truthAudit.Summary: Run 2 identified 11 findings covering 6 of 20 true vulnerabilities fully, partially addressed 5 more with severity/CWE misclassifications, and missed 9 entirely. No false-positive findings were present — all 11 previous findings were supported by the source code. The main deficiencies are missed critical/high vulnerabilities (integer overflow, use-after-free, logic bomb, path traversal, TOCTOU, data race, unbounded recursion, integer underflow, unhandled exception) and systematic severity underclaiming.

Items.Notes: Run 2 Finding 1 exactly matches the format-string injection via runtime_log_format. CWE-134, Critical severity, and evidence quote are correct.
Run 2 did not identify the integer overflow in the factorial computation (result *= i with long long overflows for inputs >= 21). No finding references fact or integer overflow.

Run 2 did not identify the use-after-free in stage_deferred_history_flush where scratch pointers allocated from g_memory_pool are captured in lambdas that execute after memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup() frees them in cleanup().
Run 2 Finding 5 correctly identifies command injection in validate_config but rates it High instead of Critical. The evidence and CWE-78 are correct; only severity is underclaimed.

Run 2 Finding 7 correctly identifies the stack buffer overflow via strcpy in evaluate_expression but rates it Medium instead of High. The CWE-120 classification is acceptable (CWE-121 is a subset). Severity is underclaimed.
Run 2 Finding 9 exactly matches the race condition in ThreadSafeCounter::increment(). CWE-362, Medium severity, and evidence are all correct.

Run 2 did not identify the logic bomb in authentication where login_attempts_ > 5 combined with EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE in the input bypasses authentication (authenticated_ = true) without valid credentials.
Run 2 did not identify path traversal in ConfigLoader::load_config where config_dir_ + filename allows directory traversal via filenames like ../../etc/passwd.

Run 2 Finding 6 correctly identifies the heap buffer overflow in ExpressionParser::parse() but rates it High instead of Critical and uses CWE-120 instead of CWE-122. The expression_buffer_ is heap-allocated from g_memory_pool, making CWE-122 more precise. Severity is underclaimed.
Run 2 Finding 2 exactly matches the hardcoded admin credentials. CWE-798, High severity, and evidence are all correct.

Run 2 Finding 10 correctly identifies weak session token generation but uses CWE-330 instead of CWE-338 and rates it Medium instead of High. The 4-digit token space (9000 values) is correctly analyzed. CWE and severity are underclaimed.
Run 2 did not identify the thread-unsafe timestamp cache in log_debug_message where static std::tm cached_time is written by localtime() without synchronization, causing a data race with CWE-362.

Run 2 Finding 4 identifies command injection in append_override_audit_event (CWE-78) but the true vulnerability is insecure temporary file handling (CWE-377) — using predictable temp-file paths derived from attacker-controllable TMPDIR/TEMP. The code path is the same but the vulnerability classification differs.
Run 2 did not identify persistent authentication state (CWE-613) where authenticated_, login_attempts_, and session_token_ persist across operations without proper session invalidation.
Run 2 did not identify the unhandled exception in handle_variable_command where std::stod(tokens[3]) can throw std::invalid_argument or std::out_of_range if tokens[3] is not a valid number.

Run 2 did not identify the integer underflow in MemoryPool::allocate where previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES can underflow when previous_size is small, causing fragment.size to wrap to a huge value.

Run 2 did not identify unbounded recursion in the parser where parse_expression calls parse_term calls parse_factor which calls parse_expression recursively on PAREN_OPEN with no depth limit checked against MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH.

Run 2 did not identify the data race in ExpressionEvaluator::evaluate_cached where result_cache_ is accessed without holding cache_mutex_ (the mutex is declared but never locked in evaluate_cached). Tasks are enqueued via thread_pool_->enqueue making this a concurrent access vulnerability.

Run 2 did not identify the TOCTOU race in ConfigLoader::load_config where std::filesystem::exists is checked, then sleep_for(25ms) occurs, then std::ifstream opens the file — allowing the file to be swapped between check and open.
Run 2 Finding 8 exactly matches the integer division by zero in calculate_route_score. CWE-369, Low severity, and evidence are all correct.
